text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Oil giant Mobile has taken state-owned Lithuanian Energy to court over what it says are unpaid debts of $4.5 million.
- Kuro Aparatura reported that its turnover was 28.4 million litas in the first half but its losses were almost one million litas.
- Lithuania expects a grain harvest of 2.6 million tonnes, of which only one million tonnes is expected to be sold.
- Central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas reiterated that Lithuania does not intend to borrow from the IMF.
- A competition to privatise Alytaus Textile will be announced in the autumn. Estonia's Hansa Investments already owns 15.5 percent of the company.
- Vilfima, top brokerage, turned over 200.8 million litas in the first half, a quarter of all turnover at the stock exchange.
- Election commission head Zenonas Vaigauskas was elected president of the association of election administrators of central and eastern Europe.
- European Affairs Minister Laime Andrikiene has agreed to stay as head of the state foreign loans commission.
- Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen will visit Lithuania on August 4, where he is expected to sign a visa-free agreement.
- The privatisation commission annulled an agreement on the sale of Zhalgiris Textile.
